1.title: Can online friendships be as deep as real ones?
1.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether friendships formed online can be as meaningful as those formed face to face. Present both sides before reaching a nuanced conclusion.
1.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si las amistades en línea pueden ser tan profundas como las presenciales.
criteria: Four phrasal verbs used naturally (strike up, fall out, grow on, come across as).
Three gerund and two infinitive constructions, including one perfect infinitive or passive gerund.
Hedged, polite disagreement (I would beg to differ, it could be argued that…).
1.model:
It is often assumed that a friendship struck up online is, by definition, shallower than one forged in a classroom or an office. I would beg to differ, although the question deserves a nuanced answer.

Sceptics argue that digital relationships lack the cues that build trust. Without seeing someone's face, it is easy to come across as warmer, funnier or more confident than one really is. Being deceived by a carefully curated profile is a genuine risk, and many people report feeling let down when an online acquaintance turns out to be quite different in person. Moreover, falling out with someone you have never met is remarkably easy: a single blocked account can end years of conversation.

Yet it could equally be argued that online spaces allow friendships to grow on us in ways that physical proximity does not. Communities built around shared passions, from chess to rare diseases, bring together people who would otherwise never have met. Many claim to have found their closest confidants in such groups, precisely because writing encourages them to open up about things they would struggle to say aloud.

On balance, the medium seems less important than the commitment. A friendship deepens when both people are willing to invest time, to listen and to forgive. Whether that happens over coffee or over a screen, what matters is being on the same wavelength. Online friendships are not inferior; they simply demand a different kind of effort to stand the test of time.

1.title: Burying the hatchet
1.brief: Write an email to a friend you fell out with years ago, proposing a reconciliation. Acknowledge what went wrong without sounding defensive.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo con quien te peleaste hace años proponiendo una reconciliación sin sonar a la defensiva.
criteria: Four phrasal verbs or idioms from the unit, including to bury the hatchet.
A perfect infinitive (seem to have…) and a passive gerund (being left out).
A tone that balances warmth and accountability.
1.model:
Dear Mateo,

I have started this email at least a dozen times, so forgive me if it comes out a little clumsily.

It has been almost four years since we fell out over the business we were planning together, and I have come to realise that I handled the whole situation badly. At the time, I was convinced you had let me down. Looking back, I seem to have ignored how much pressure you were under, and I certainly did nothing to make you feel heard. I remember you saying that you hated being left out of decisions, and you were right: I kept making them without you.

I am not writing to reopen old arguments. I simply miss having you around. We hit it off from the very first week of university, and I don't think I have been on the same wavelength with anyone quite like that since. It seems absurd to have let one failed project end a friendship of ten years.

If you are open to it, I would love to bury the hatchet over a coffee — or a beer, if that feels more appropriate. I'm back in Medellín for the whole of next month, so I could easily fit around your schedule. And if you would rather not, I completely understand; I would still be glad to have finally said this.

Take care, and say hello to your parents for me.

Warmly,
Santiago

1.title: Review: a film about friendship
1.brief: Write a review for a cultural website of a film, series or novel that explores friendship. Analyse how the relationship develops and evaluate how convincingly it is portrayed.
1.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una película, serie o novela sobre la amistad, analizando cómo evoluciona la relación.
criteria: Four phrasal verbs describing the relationship (hit it off, drift apart, grow on, fall out).
A variety of gerund and infinitive patterns after verbs and adjectives.
Clear evaluation with a final recommendation.
1.model:
The Banshees of Inisherin (2022) begins with one of the most unsettling premises in recent cinema: one morning, Colm simply decides to stop being friends with Pádraic. There is no argument, no betrayal — only Colm's announcement that he no longer wishes to waste his remaining years on dull conversation.

What follows is a darkly comic and ultimately tragic study of what happens when two people drift apart for reasons only one of them understands. Pádraic, played with heartbreaking innocence by Colin Farrell, refuses to accept being cast aside. His attempts to win Colm back grow increasingly desperate, and Colm's determination to be left alone becomes frighteningly extreme.

Director Martin McDonagh avoids explaining too much. We never learn exactly when the two men hit it off or how long their friendship has lasted, yet the film manages to convey decades of shared routine in a few glances. The bleak island landscape seems to have been chosen to mirror their isolation, and the civil war raging across the water is a clever parallel to their private conflict.

The film is not without flaws. Its pace may test viewers who expect a conventional plot, and some of the secondary characters feel underdeveloped. However, the central performances are extraordinary, and the story grows on you long after the credits roll.

I would strongly recommend it to anyone interested in the fragility of adult friendship — though perhaps not as light entertainment for a Friday night.

2.title: Dress codes at work: necessary or outdated?
2.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether companies should still impose dress codes on their employees.
2.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si las empresas deberían seguir imponiendo códigos de vestimenta.
criteria: Two cleft sentences with what (What many managers fear is…).
Varied verb patterns (expect someone to, object to + -ing, make someone feel).
Three expressions from the unit (to dress down, to look the part, understated).
2.model:
Few workplace policies provoke as much debate as the dress code. While some organisations still require suits and ties, a growing number now allow employees to dress down every day. Which approach is more justified?

Supporters of formal dress codes argue that clothing communicates professionalism. A lawyer who turns up in trainers may struggle to look the part in front of a client, however competent she is. What many managers fear is that relaxed rules will gradually erode standards and blur the line between work and leisure. Uniforms, moreover, can create a sense of equality, preventing staff from competing over expensive brands.

Critics, however, object to being told what to wear, particularly when the rules are applied unequally. Women are frequently expected to wear heels or make-up, while men are not, and religious or cultural dress may be treated as "unprofessional". What research increasingly shows is that people who feel comfortable are more productive and more creative. Being forced into an uncomfortable suit in a city as hot as Barranquilla hardly makes anyone work better.

In my view, the most sensible solution lies somewhere in between. Rather than imposing rigid codes, companies could set broad guidelines — clean, appropriate, understated — and trust employees to adapt them to the context. A sales representative meeting a bank's directors will naturally dress differently from a programmer working remotely. What matters ultimately is not the tie, but the quality of the work.

2.title: A wardrobe that tells my story
2.brief: Write a personal article for a lifestyle magazine about one item of clothing that has special meaning for you and what it reveals about who you are.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo personal sobre una prenda con significado especial y lo que revela de ti.
criteria: Two or three cleft sentences with what or all (What I love about it is…).
Five different verb patterns (remind someone to, can’t help + -ing, stop + -ing / to).
Use “hand-me-downs”, “timeless” or “to pull off”.
2.model:
Most of my clothes come and go without leaving a trace. One, however, has followed me for fifteen years: a faded brown leather jacket that once belonged to my grandfather.

It came to me, like many of my childhood clothes, as a hand-me-down. My grandfather wore it on his motorbike in the 1970s, and when he stopped riding, it was hung in a wardrobe and forgotten. I found it at sixteen, put it on and refused to take it off. It was far too big, and my mother warned me that I would never pull it off. I wore it anyway.

What I love about it is not its style, although it has a timeless quality that no fast-fashion jacket could imitate. What really matters is the way it makes me feel. Whenever I wear it, I can't help remembering the stories he used to tell about crossing the Andes on that bike. It reminds me to take risks, to travel and to stay curious.

The jacket has been repaired several times. The lining has been replaced, and one sleeve bears a scar from a fall I would rather not discuss. Friends occasionally suggest I buy a new one. What they don't understand is that the wear is the whole point.

All I hope is that, one day, it will fit someone else in the family just as badly as it once fitted me.

2.title: First impressions in job interviews
2.brief: Write an article for a careers website advising young professionals on how appearance influences first impressions in interviews, and how to manage it without losing authenticity.
2.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para un portal de empleo sobre cómo la apariencia influye en la primera impresión en entrevistas.
criteria: Two cleft sentences with what and one with it (It is… that…).
A range of verb patterns (advise someone to, avoid + -ing, end up + -ing).
Use “to judge a book by its cover” and “to be dressed to the nines”.
2.model:
Dressing for Success — Without Disappearing

We are told not to judge a book by its cover, yet research suggests that interviewers form an opinion within the first seven seconds of meeting a candidate. Appearance is, inevitably, part of that impression.

What recruiters look for, above all, is appropriateness. Turning up dressed to the nines for an interview at a relaxed tech startup can be just as damaging as wearing jeans to a meeting at a law firm. It is the mismatch, rather than the clothes themselves, that sends the wrong signal: it suggests you have not done your research. Before the interview, take time to look at the company's social media and notice how employees present themselves.

Experts generally advise candidates to aim one level above the everyday dress of the workplace. If the team wears T-shirts, a smart shirt is enough; if they wear blazers, choose a suit. Avoid wearing anything you have not tried on beforehand — many people end up spending the entire interview adjusting a tight collar or uncomfortable shoes.

What is often overlooked, however, is authenticity. You do not need to erase your personality to be taken seriously. A distinctive pair of glasses or a piece of traditional jewellery can make you memorable, provided it does not distract from what you are saying.

Finally, remember that clothes open the door, but it is your preparation that keeps it open. Confidence comes from knowing your subject, not from the label on your jacket.

3.title: Should AI be used to mark students' work?
3.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether artificial intelligence should be used to grade essays and exams in schools and universities.
3.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si la inteligencia artificial debería usarse para calificar exámenes y ensayos.
criteria: Accurate use of articles (a / the / zero article) with abstract and specific nouns.
Three -ing clauses (Having analysed…, Using algorithms, …).
Four expressions from the unit (cutting-edge, drawback, unintended consequences, to roll out).
3.model:
In recent years, a number of universities have begun to roll out software that uses artificial intelligence to grade students' work. Supporters describe it as a game-changer; critics see it as a threat to education itself.

The advantages are considerable. Marking hundreds of essays is exhausting, and tired teachers are not always consistent. Using cutting-edge language models, a computer can assess grammar, structure and argument in seconds, providing instant feedback that students can act on immediately. Freed from repetitive grading, teachers would have more time for the human side of teaching: explaining, motivating and listening.

However, the drawbacks are equally serious. Algorithms are trained on existing data, which means they may reward conventional writing and penalise originality. Having been designed mainly in English-speaking countries, many systems also struggle with the varieties of English used by students in Latin America or Asia. Perhaps the greatest danger lies in the unintended consequences: if students know that a machine is reading their work, they may simply learn to write for the machine, producing formulaic texts that tick the right boxes.

Weighing up these arguments, I believe that AI should play a supporting role rather than a decisive one. It can be a valuable tool for checking drafts and spotting errors, but the final grade — and the judgement about what makes an idea genuinely interesting — should remain in human hands. Education is, after all, a relationship between people, not merely the processing of data.

3.title: A report on technology use at work
3.brief: Your manager has asked you to write a report on how a new piece of technology (a chatbot, a project-management app, video conferencing) has affected your team, with recommendations.
3.briefEs: Escribe un informe para tu jefe sobre el impacto de una nueva tecnología en tu equipo, con recomendaciones.
criteria: Headings and an impersonal, formal register.
Three -ing clauses for concision (Comparing the figures, …).
Correct articles with general vs specific references (the software, technology in general).
3.model:
Report: Impact of the Customer-Service Chatbot

Introduction
This report evaluates the chatbot introduced in our customer-service department in March and makes recommendations for its future use. It is based on usage data and interviews with twelve members of staff.

Findings
Comparing the figures for the first and second quarters, the average waiting time for customers fell from eleven minutes to three. The chatbot now resolves approximately 40% of enquiries without human intervention, mostly simple requests such as changing passwords or checking the status of an order.

However, several problems were identified. Having been trained on generic data, the software frequently misunderstands regional expressions, which has led to a number of frustrated customers. Staff also reported that complaints transferred from the chatbot tend to be more complex and emotionally charged, increasing pressure on the team. Two employees described feeling that their role had become "damage control".

Recommendations
• The chatbot should be retrained using transcripts of real conversations with Colombian customers.
• Customers should be offered the option of speaking to a person at any stage, rather than only after three failed attempts.
• Training in handling difficult calls should be provided for all agents.
• The system's performance should be reviewed again in six months.

Conclusion
Overall, the technology has delivered clear gains in efficiency. Nevertheless, unless the issues outlined above are addressed, there is a risk that customer satisfaction and staff morale will decline.

3.title: The invention that changed my family's life
3.brief: Write an article for a science magazine's readers' section about a technology (old or new) that transformed your family's daily life.
3.briefEs: Escribe un artículo para la sección de lectores de una revista científica sobre una tecnología que transformó la vida de tu familia.
criteria: Precise use of the definite article for inventions and institutions (the washing machine, the internet).
Three -ing clauses, including one perfect (Having lived…).
Use “breakthrough”, “obsolete” and “to render obsolete”.
3.model:
When people talk about technological breakthroughs, they usually mention the internet or the smartphone. For my family, the revolution was far humbler: a solar panel.

My grandparents live on a small farm in the mountains of Cauca, two hours from the nearest town. Having lived without a reliable electricity supply for most of their lives, they organised their days around the sun. Cooking was done with firewood, homework was done before dark, and the only radio ran on batteries that were expensive and hard to find.

In 2017, a government programme installed a set of solar panels on their roof. The change was immediate. Using a single panel and a battery, they could suddenly light the house, charge a phone and run a small fridge. My grandmother began selling cheese and milk to neighbours, keeping them cool for the first time. My younger cousins, studying by electric light, saw their grades improve.

The panels did not render the old ways obsolete overnight. My grandfather still prefers to cook on the wood stove, insisting that the food tastes better. Yet the technology has transformed what is possible in a place the national grid has never reached.

What strikes me most is how little attention such innovations receive. We celebrate the latest phone, but for millions of rural families, the real game-changer is the ability to switch on a light.

4.title: Why do intelligent people believe in superstitions?
4.brief: Write a discursive essay exploring why superstitions persist in modern, educated societies, and whether they do any harm.
4.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre por qué persisten las supersticiones en sociedades modernas y si hacen daño.
criteria: Four reporting verbs with that-clauses or infinitives (claim, argue, suggest, maintain).
Two passive reporting structures (It is believed that…, X is said to…).
Use “anecdotal”, “to debunk” and “to lend credence to”.
4.model:
In an age of space exploration and genetic engineering, it might seem surprising that millions of people still avoid walking under ladders or refuse to fly on Friday the 13th. Yet superstitions remain remarkably persistent, even among the highly educated.

Psychologists suggest that superstitions offer a sense of control in situations that are inherently uncertain. Athletes are known to follow elaborate rituals before competitions; tennis star Rafael Nadal, for instance, is said to arrange his water bottles in exactly the same position at every match. It is widely believed that such routines reduce anxiety, which may in turn improve performance — lending credence, ironically, to the idea that the ritual "works".

Others argue that superstitions are simply cultural habits passed down through generations. In Colombia, many families still burn sage on New Year's Eve or walk around the block with a suitcase to guarantee travel. Few genuinely believe in these customs, but they maintain that abandoning them would feel like breaking a link with their grandparents.

Most superstitions are harmless, and some may even be beneficial. However, problems arise when people base serious decisions on anecdotal evidence. Rejecting medical treatment in favour of a lucky charm, or refusing to vaccinate a child because of an omen, can have tragic consequences. Scientists have debunked countless such beliefs, but debunking alone rarely changes behaviour.

Ultimately, superstition seems to be part of human nature. The challenge is not to eliminate it, but to ensure it never takes the place of reason.

4.title: A report on a viral claim
4.brief: Write a fact-checking report for a news website on a viral claim (a miracle cure, a conspiracy theory, a fake celebrity quote). Report what was claimed, by whom, and what the evidence shows.
4.briefEs: Escribe un informe de verificación de datos sobre una afirmación viral: qué se dijo, quién lo dijo y qué muestran las pruebas.
criteria: Five different reporting verbs (claim, allege, deny, insist, acknowledge).
Three passive reporting clauses (It has been suggested that…, is thought to have…).
An objective, neutral register.
4.model:
FACT CHECK: Does Lemon Water Cure Diabetes?

A video claiming that drinking hot lemon water every morning can cure type 2 diabetes has been shared more than three million times on social media in the past week.

The claim
In the video, a man who describes himself as a "natural health expert" alleges that he cured his own diabetes in thirty days by drinking lemon water and avoiding all medication. He insists that doctors hide this "secret" because pharmaceutical companies would lose money. The video is thought to have originated on a Brazilian channel before being translated into Spanish.

What the evidence shows
We consulted three endocrinologists and reviewed the scientific literature. While lemon juice is a healthy drink, there is no evidence that it can cure diabetes. It has been suggested in some small studies that citrus fruits may slightly reduce blood sugar spikes after meals, but researchers acknowledge that these effects are minimal. Dr. Ana Lucía Barrios of the Colombian Diabetes Association warned that patients who stop taking their medication risk serious complications, including kidney failure and blindness.

When contacted, the author of the video denied that he was giving medical advice, claiming that he was simply "sharing his experience". The account has since been removed by the platform.

Verdict: FALSE
Lemon water is not a cure for diabetes. Patients should never stop prescribed treatment without consulting a doctor.

4.title: Lucky charms and rituals
4.brief: Write a blog post about the superstitions and rituals in your family or region. Report what people say about them and reflect on why you keep (or reject) them.
4.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de blog sobre las supersticiones de tu familia o región y reflexiona por qué las mantienes o rechazas.
criteria: Reporting verbs with different patterns (warn someone not to, swear that, be supposed to).
Two passive reporting structures (is believed to, is said to bring).
Use “far-fetched”, “gullible”, “to take something at face value”.
4.model:
My Grandmother's Rules for a Lucky Life

Growing up in Popayán, I learned that luck was something you had to work for — or at least something you could protect through a long list of rules, mostly invented by my grandmother.

She warned us never to put a handbag on the floor, because doing so is believed to make your money "run away". She swore that a black butterfly in the house announced bad news, and that if your left hand itched, you were about to receive money. On New Year's Eve, we were supposed to eat twelve grapes at midnight, one for each wish, and wear yellow underwear for good fortune. A sábila (aloe vera) plant hung behind the front door is said to keep envy away; we had three.

As a teenager, I found all this far-fetched. I accused my family of being gullible and refused to eat the grapes, which my grandmother took as a personal insult. These days, my attitude has softened. I don't take any of these beliefs at face value, but I have started to see them as a kind of family language — a way of expressing hope and fear without having to name them.

So yes, I still hang a sábila behind my door. I don't think it protects me from envy. But every time I see it, I think of her, and that feels like a kind of luck in itself.

5.title: Has streaming killed the cinema?
5.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether streaming platforms are destroying the cinema-going experience or giving it new life.
5.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si las plataformas de streaming están destruyendo el cine o dándole nueva vida.
criteria: Four sentence adverbs (admittedly, arguably, undeniably, ultimately).
Two “such…that” or “so…that” structures.
Use “blockbuster”, “to binge-watch” and “critically acclaimed”.
5.model:
When the first streaming platforms appeared, few people imagined that they would one day release more films than Hollywood's traditional studios. Today, the question is no longer whether streaming will change cinema, but whether cinemas themselves will survive.

Undeniably, the convenience of streaming has transformed viewing habits. Audiences can binge-watch an entire series in a weekend without leaving the sofa, and the cost of a monthly subscription is lower than that of two cinema tickets. The pandemic accelerated this trend so dramatically that many cinemas never reopened. Arguably, platforms have also democratised filmmaking: directors from Colombia, Nigeria or Korea now reach global audiences that would have been unthinkable twenty years ago.

Admittedly, something is lost along the way. Watching a film on a phone, interrupted by notifications, is hardly the experience its creators intended. The collective emotion of a full cinema — laughing, gasping, crying together — cannot be reproduced at home. Moreover, algorithms tend to promote content similar to what we have already seen, so that risky, original projects struggle to find funding.

Yet cinemas are not dead. Big-screen blockbusters still break box-office records, and many critically acclaimed films owe their success to a theatrical release that generates conversation. Some cinemas have reinvented themselves with such comfortable seats and such carefully curated programmes that going out has become an event once again.

Ultimately, streaming and cinema seem destined to coexist, each offering something the other cannot.

5.title: A TV series pitch
5.brief: Write a proposal to a streaming platform for a new series set in Colombia. Describe the premise, the genre, the target audience and why it would be successful.
5.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta a una plataforma de streaming para una nueva serie ambientada en Colombia.
criteria: Headings: Premise, Characters, Audience, Why it will work.
Two sentence adverbs and one “so…that” structure.
Use “plot twist”, “gripping” and “to suspend disbelief”.
5.model:
Proposal: "Los Guardianes del Páramo" — a six-episode thriller

Premise
When a young hydrologist arrives in a remote village in the Sumapaz páramo to study its water supply, she discovers that several local leaders have disappeared. As she investigates, she uncovers a conflict between a mining company, armed groups and an indigenous community determined to protect the largest páramo on Earth.

Characters
The protagonist, Laura, is brilliant but socially awkward, and her outsider's perspective allows viewers to discover the region through her eyes. She is joined by Don Efraín, a farmer whose knowledge of the mountains is so deep that he becomes her indispensable guide.

Audience
The series targets viewers aged 18–45 who enjoy socially conscious thrillers such as "Narcos" or "Frontera Verde", as well as international audiences interested in Latin American stories.

Why it will work
Crucially, the series combines a gripping mystery with stunning, rarely filmed landscapes. Each episode ends with a plot twist designed to keep viewers watching. Unlike many crime dramas, it never asks the audience to suspend disbelief: the story is based on real environmental conflicts, carefully researched with local experts. Interestingly, recent surveys show a growing global demand for stories about climate and nature.

Budget and timeline
We estimate filming would take four months, with a budget of USD 6 million. We would be delighted to present a full script of the pilot episode.

5.title: Overrated: a dissenting review
5.brief: Write a review of a very popular film or series that you consider overrated. Argue your position respectfully and acknowledge its strengths.
5.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una película o serie muy popular que consideras sobrevalorada, reconociendo sus fortalezas.
criteria: Four sentence adverbs to signal stance (frankly, admittedly, curiously, regrettably).
Two “such…that” or “so…that” sentences.
Use “overrated”, “hit and miss” and “to give away”.
5.model:
It may be the most-watched series in Netflix's history, but Squid Game left me strangely cold.

Admittedly, its premise is brilliant. Hundreds of people drowning in debt are invited to compete in children's games for an enormous cash prize, only to discover that losing means death. The contrast between the brightly coloured sets and the brutal violence is so striking that the first episode is genuinely unforgettable. Lee Jung-jae, as the gambling-addicted protagonist, delivers a performance of remarkable vulnerability.

Regrettably, the series fails to sustain that early promise. After the initial shock, the structure becomes predictable: a new game, a few deaths, a moment of betrayal, repeat. The secondary storyline involving a police officer is so poorly developed that it feels like padding. Frankly, several episodes could have been cut without losing anything essential.

More importantly, the social criticism, which many viewers praised, is surprisingly superficial. The show tells us repeatedly that capitalism is cruel, yet it rarely explores why its characters ended up in such desperate situations. Curiously, the VIPs — the wealthy spectators who represent the system — are written so badly that they become almost comic. Without giving away the ending, I found the final twist more confusing than shocking.

Is it worth watching? Probably, if only to understand a global phenomenon. But for me, Squid Game is hit and miss: visually stunning and occasionally powerful, yet ultimately overrated.

6.title: Should streaming services pay musicians more?
6.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether music streaming platforms treat artists fairly and what should change.
6.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si las plataformas de música tratan justamente a los artistas.
criteria: Two double comparatives (The more…, the more…).
One use of will / would for characteristic habits.
Use “to go viral”, “a one-hit wonder” and “to sell out”.
6.model:
Never has music been so accessible. For the price of a lunch, listeners can enjoy almost every song ever recorded. Yet many musicians argue that this abundance has come at their expense.

The figures are striking. Platforms typically pay artists between 0.003 and 0.005 dollars per stream, which means that a song must be played around 250,000 times to earn the equivalent of a monthly minimum salary in Colombia. The more songs are uploaded every day — currently over 100,000 — the harder it becomes for independent musicians to stand out. Many will spend years releasing music that nobody hears, while a handful of global stars receive the vast majority of royalties.

Defenders of streaming point out that it has rescued an industry devastated by piracy. Artists who would once have depended on record labels can now reach audiences directly, and a song can go viral overnight, turning an unknown singer into a star. However, critics reply that this model encourages short, catchy tracks designed for algorithms, producing a generation of one-hit wonders rather than lasting careers.

In my view, the system needs reform. A "user-centric" payment model, in which each subscriber's money goes only to the artists they actually listen to, would be fairer to niche musicians. Platforms could also give more visibility to local talent. The more value listeners place on music, the more willing they should be to pay for it. Artists should not have to sell out to survive.

6.title: The concert I'll never forget
6.brief: Write a narrative for a music magazine's readers' section about a concert or musical experience that had a lasting impact on you.
6.briefEs: Escribe una narración sobre un concierto o experiencia musical que te marcó.
criteria: One or two double comparatives (the longer…, the louder…).
Two uses of would or will for habitual behaviour.
Use “to strike a chord”, “lyrics” and “catchy”.
6.model:
I was fourteen when my father took me to see Carlos Vives at the Parque Simón Bolívar. I had protested all week. Back then, I only listened to American pop, and vallenato, as far as I was concerned, was the music my uncles would play at family parties until three in the morning.

We arrived early, squeezed between thousands of people waving Colombian flags. When the first accordion notes rang out, I rolled my eyes. But something strange happened. The longer the concert went on, the less I wanted to pretend I wasn't enjoying it. The rhythm was catchy, of course, but it was the lyrics that struck a chord — songs about the Sierra Nevada, the rivers and the small towns my father had grown up in.

At one point, Vives sang "La Tierra del Olvido", and I looked at my father. He was crying. I had never seen him cry before. He told me later that his own father used to sing that song while working in the fields.

That night changed my relationship with music. The more I listened to vallenato and cumbia, the more I understood where I came from. These days, I will often put on an old Diomedes Díaz album while I cook, and my American pop playlists gather dust.

My father still teases me about it. "You came for me," he says, "but you stayed for the accordion."

6.title: What defines musical success?
6.brief: Write an article for a cultural website discussing what “success” means for a musician today: fame, money, critical acclaim or longevity.
6.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre qué significa el éxito para un músico hoy: fama, dinero, crítica o permanencia.
criteria: Two double comparatives and one “would” for past habits.
Use “to fade into obscurity”, “to stand the test of time” and “derivative”.
A title, clear sections or paragraphs, and a thought-provoking ending.
6.model:
What Does It Mean to "Make It" in Music?

Ask a teenager what makes a musician successful, and the answer will probably be measured in numbers: followers, streams, views. Yet the history of music suggests that numbers alone tell a very incomplete story.

Consider fame. Every year, dozens of songs go viral and accumulate billions of plays, only for their creators to fade into obscurity within months. The faster an artist rises, it often seems, the faster they fall. Money is an equally unreliable measure. Many of the highest-earning performers today produce music that critics dismiss as derivative, while some of the most influential artists in history died poor. Van Gogh's story has musical equivalents: Nick Drake, for instance, sold fewer than 5,000 albums in his lifetime and is now regarded as a genius.

Critical acclaim offers another perspective, but critics are not infallible. In the 1960s, many reviewers would describe rock and roll as noise that would never last.

Perhaps the truest test of success is longevity: music that stands the test of time. Songs by Totó la Momposina or Joe Arroyo continue to fill dance floors decades after they were recorded, not because an algorithm recommends them, but because they still mean something to people.

The more I think about it, the more convinced I become that success cannot be reduced to a single metric. A musician who moves a small audience deeply may have achieved more than one who entertains millions briefly. Fame is loud; influence is quiet — and it lasts much longer.

7.title: Is nostalgia holding us back?
7.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether nostalgia for “the good old days” is harmless comfort or an obstacle to progress.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si la nostalgia por “los viejos tiempos” es un consuelo inofensivo o un obstáculo.
criteria: Relative clauses where the pronoun is optional and where it is required (omitted in at least one).
Two comparisons with as if / as though / the way / like.
Use “nostalgia”, “to hark back to” and “with hindsight”.
7.model:
Every generation seems convinced that life was better before. Our grandparents talk about the days when neighbours left their doors open; our parents remember a childhood without screens. But is this nostalgia a harmless pleasure, or does it prevent us from embracing change?

There is no doubt that nostalgia serves a purpose. Psychologists have found that recalling happy memories can reduce loneliness and give people a sense of continuity in a world that changes at bewildering speed. The songs we listened to as teenagers, the food our mothers cooked, the streets we played in — these connect us to who we were. Speaking about the past the way our elders do is also a means of passing values from one generation to the next.

However, nostalgia can distort reality. Many people talk about the 1980s as if they had been a golden age, forgetting the violence, the inequality and the lack of opportunities that characterised those years in Colombia. With hindsight, the past often looks simpler than it really was, simply because we were children and others solved our problems for us. Politicians who hark back to an idealised past frequently use this sentiment to resist necessary reforms, from women's rights to environmental protection.

The healthiest approach, it seems to me, is to treat nostalgia like a photograph rather than a map. We can look at it with affection, but we should not use it to decide where to go next. The past we remember is, after all, partly one we have invented.

7.title: A milestone that shaped me
7.brief: Write a reflective personal essay about a rite of passage or milestone that marked your transition into adulthood.
7.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo personal reflexivo sobre un rito de paso o hito que marcó tu entrada a la adultez.
criteria: Three relative clauses, including one with the pronoun omitted and one with a preposition (in which / whom).
Two clauses with as if, as though or like.
Use “a rite of passage”, “formative” and “to look back on”.
7.model:
In many cultures, the rite of passage into adulthood is a ceremony: a quinceañera, a graduation, a first communion. Mine was far less glamorous. It was the night I spent alone in a hospital waiting room at the age of nineteen.

My mother, with whom I had always had a difficult relationship, collapsed at work and was taken to the emergency room. My father was travelling, and my older brother lived abroad, so the decisions the doctors needed fell to me. I remember signing forms I barely understood, talking to nurses as though I knew what I was doing, and calling relatives in a voice that sounded like someone else's.

She recovered, thankfully. But something had shifted. For the first time, I saw my mother not as an authority figure but as a person who was vulnerable and frightened, just like me. In the weeks that followed, we talked in a way we never had before.

When I look back on that period, I realise how formative it was. The person I had been — impatient, convinced that my parents owed me everything — did not survive that night. In his place was someone who understood that caring for others is not a burden but a responsibility we inherit.

People sometimes describe adulthood as if it were a destination you reach at eighteen. In my experience, it arrives without warning, in a corridor that smells of disinfectant, at three o'clock in the morning.

7.title: The generation gap at work
7.brief: Write a report for a company's human resources department on the challenges and benefits of having several generations working together, with recommendations.
7.briefEs: Escribe un informe para recursos humanos sobre los retos y beneficios de que varias generaciones trabajen juntas.
criteria: Headings, impersonal register and recommendations.
Relative clauses with required and optional pronouns, including “whose”.
Use “generation gap” and one structure with “the way”.
7.model:
Report: Managing a Multigenerational Workforce

Introduction
The aim of this report is to examine how the generation gap affects collaboration in our company, in which employees range in age from 19 to 67. It draws on a staff survey and four focus groups.

Challenges
The main difficulties identified relate to communication. Older employees, whose careers began before email, generally prefer face-to-face meetings and phone calls, whereas younger staff favour instant messaging. Several participants complained about the way colleagues of other ages reply to messages, describing them as either "too formal" or "rude". There are also differing expectations regarding working hours: the flexibility that younger employees value is sometimes perceived by senior managers as a lack of commitment.

Benefits
Despite these tensions, mixed teams were found to perform better on complex projects. Employees with decades of experience contribute knowledge of clients and industry history that cannot be learned from manuals, while recent graduates bring digital skills and fresh perspectives. Many respondents said the colleague they had learned most from was someone from a different generation.

Recommendations
• A reverse mentoring scheme should be introduced, in which junior staff teach digital tools to senior colleagues and vice versa.
• Teams should agree explicitly on preferred communication channels and response times.
• Training on unconscious age bias should be offered to all managers.

Conclusion
Age diversity is an asset which, if managed thoughtfully, can strengthen both innovation and staff loyalty.

8.title: Is advertising to children ethical?
8.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether advertising aimed at children should be banned or more strictly regulated.
8.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si la publicidad dirigida a niños debería prohibirse o regularse más.
criteria: Two subjunctive structures (It is essential that companies be…, insist that…).
Correct placement of direct and indirect objects (sell children products / sell products to children).
Use “target audience”, “consumerism” and “brand loyalty”.
8.model:
Children have become one of the most lucrative target audiences in the world. Companies spend billions every year trying to sell them products, from sugary cereals to video games, and to build brand loyalty that will last a lifetime. Should this be allowed?

Those who defend children's advertising argue that it is a legitimate part of a market economy. Adverts inform families about new products, and they fund much of the free content children enjoy, from television programmes to online videos. Moreover, they insist that parents, not governments, should decide what their children are exposed to.

However, this argument overlooks a crucial fact: young children cannot distinguish between entertainment and persuasion. Research suggests that, until about the age of eight, most children believe that adverts simply tell the truth. Promoting junk food to them has been linked to rising rates of childhood obesity, and influencers who show children toys in "unboxing" videos often fail to make clear that they are being paid. Encouraging consumerism from such an early age also places enormous pressure on low-income families, whose children may feel excluded when they cannot buy what their friends have.

In my view, it is essential that advertising to young children be strictly regulated. Several countries, including Chile and Norway, have already banned marketing unhealthy food to under-14s, with encouraging results. I would recommend that Colombia adopt similar measures, and that platforms be required to label sponsored content clearly. Childhood should be a time for play, not a marketing opportunity.

8.title: Review: a product that didn't live up to the hype
8.brief: Write a detailed review for a consumer website of a product you bought because of clever marketing, explaining why it was a false economy.
8.briefEs: Escribe una reseña para un sitio de consumidores sobre un producto que compraste por el marketing y resultó mala inversión.
criteria: Two sentences with indirect objects in different positions (gave me a discount / gave it to me).
One subjunctive (I would suggest that buyers be…).
Use “impulse buy”, “to be sold on” and “a false economy”.
8.model:
★★☆☆☆ "The last blender you'll ever need" — or not

I'll admit it: this blender was an impulse buy. I was scrolling late at night when an advert showed me a smiling chef crushing ice, nuts and frozen fruit in seconds. A countdown timer promised me a 40% discount if I ordered within ten minutes. I was sold on it before I had even read the specifications.

The first week was promising. The design is elegant and the machine is surprisingly quiet. However, problems appeared quickly. The jug is made of thin plastic that cracked after a month of daily smoothies, and the "powerful" motor struggles with anything harder than a banana. When I contacted customer service, they offered me a replacement jug — but only if I paid the shipping, which cost almost as much as the jug itself.

What frustrates me most is the marketing. The "40% discount" turned out to be the product's normal price; the timer resets every time you open the page. The lifetime guarantee that the website advertises applies only to the motor, and only if you register within seven days.

In the end, this cheap blender proved a false economy. I have since bought a sturdier model from a well-known brand, which cost twice as much but has worked perfectly for a year.

My advice: ignore the countdown timers. I would suggest that buyers be especially wary of products sold exclusively through social media adverts.

8.title: A letter to the editor about consumerism
8.brief: Write a letter to a newspaper editor responding to an article that praised Black Friday as “good for the economy”. Present a counter-argument.
8.briefEs: Escribe una carta al editor respondiendo a un artículo que elogiaba el Black Friday como “bueno para la economía”.
criteria: Formal letter conventions and a clear position.
Two subjunctive structures (I propose that…, It is vital that…).
Use “disposable income”, “to drive up” and “consumerism”.
8.model:
Dear Editor,

I read with interest last Sunday's article "Black Friday: A Gift for the Economy", in which your columnist argued that the annual shopping event benefits Colombian businesses and consumers alike. While I do not dispute that retailers enjoy a surge in sales, I believe the article presented a dangerously incomplete picture.

Firstly, many of the so-called bargains are illusory. Consumer organisations have repeatedly shown that some shops drive up prices in the weeks before the event in order to offer apparently spectacular discounts. Secondly, the pressure to buy encourages families to spend money they do not have. For households with little disposable income, credit-card debt taken on in November can last well into the following year.

There is also an environmental cost that the article ignored entirely. Much of what is purchased — cheap electronics, fast fashion — is discarded within months, contributing to the mountains of waste our cities already struggle to manage.

I am not suggesting that shopping is inherently wrong. However, a newspaper that celebrates unrestrained consumerism without acknowledging its consequences does its readers a disservice. I propose that your paper publish practical advice on recognising false discounts, and it is vital that the government require shops to display the lowest price charged in the previous thirty days, as is now the rule in the European Union.

Yours faithfully,
Mariana Ochoa
Bucaramanga

9.title: Should we bring back extinct species?
9.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether scientists should use genetic technology to bring extinct species back to life.
9.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si los científicos deberían revivir especies extintas con tecnología genética.
criteria: Two noun clauses with whoever / whatever (Whatever the benefits, …).
One contrast between whenever / wherever and when / where.
Use “biodiversity”, “ecosystem” and “to be on the brink of”.
9.model:
In 2025, a biotechnology company announced that it had created mice with the woolly coat of a mammoth, and that it intended to bring the mammoth itself back to life within a decade. "De-extinction", once the stuff of science fiction, is now a serious scientific project. But should it be?

Supporters argue that reviving lost species could restore damaged ecosystems. Mammoths, for example, once trampled the Arctic snow and kept the permafrost frozen; their return might slow the release of greenhouse gases. Whoever has seen a museum skeleton of a dodo can understand the emotional appeal of undoing humanity's past mistakes. Moreover, the techniques developed could help species that are on the brink of extinction today, by increasing their genetic diversity.

Opponents, however, raise powerful objections. Whatever the scientific achievement, a single cloned animal is not a species: it has no parents to learn from and no habitat that still exists in its original form. Wherever such creatures were released, they could behave unpredictably and threaten the animals that live there now. Perhaps the strongest argument is economic. The millions spent on de-extinction could protect thousands of hectares of rainforest, where biodiversity is being lost every day.

In my opinion, the research should continue, but only as a tool for conservation, not as a spectacle. When a species disappears, the real lesson is that prevention is far cheaper than resurrection. Whoever controls this technology must remember that the best way to save an animal is not to lose it in the first place.

9.title: A proposal for protecting a local habitat
9.brief: Write a proposal to your local council or an environmental fund for a project to protect a habitat in your region (a wetland, a river, a forest).
9.briefEs: Escribe una propuesta al concejo local o a un fondo ambiental para proteger un hábitat de tu región.
criteria: Headings: Background, Objectives, Proposed actions, Budget, Expected outcomes.
One noun clause with whoever or whatever and one clause with whenever / wherever.
Use “habitat”, “to encroach on” and “resilience”.
9.model:
Proposal: Restoring the Juan Amarillo Wetland

Background
The Juan Amarillo wetland in north-west Bogotá is home to more than 100 species of birds, including the endemic Bogotá rail. Over the past thirty years, however, housing developments have encroached on the wetland, reducing its area by almost 40%. Pollution from illegal waste dumping and untreated sewage threatens what remains.

Objectives
The project aims to restore the wetland's natural habitat, improve water quality and involve local residents in its long-term protection.

Proposed actions
1. Planting 5,000 native trees and aquatic plants along the edges of the wetland to strengthen the ecosystem's resilience.
2. Installing filters at the three main points where wastewater enters.
3. Creating a volunteer "guardians" programme. Whoever joins will receive training in bird monitoring and environmental education.
4. Placing information boards and bins wherever visitors gather, and organising monthly clean-up days.

Budget
We request COP 180 million over two years, of which 60% would be allocated to restoration work, 25% to water treatment and 15% to community activities.

Expected outcomes
Within two years, we expect a measurable increase in bird populations and a significant reduction in waste. Whatever the final figures, the programme will have created a network of residents committed to the wetland's future, which is perhaps its most lasting benefit.

Conclusion
Wetlands are among the most valuable — and most threatened — ecosystems in the city. Protecting Juan Amarillo now will cost far less than restoring it later.

9.title: An encounter with wildlife
9.brief: Write a narrative for a nature magazine about a memorable encounter with an animal in the wild, and reflect on what it taught you about conservation.
9.briefEs: Escribe una narración para una revista de naturaleza sobre un encuentro memorable con un animal salvaje.
criteria: One clause with whenever or wherever and one noun clause with whatever.
Vivid descriptive language and a reflective ending.
Use “endangered”, “to poach” or “conservation”.
9.model:
We had been sitting in the canoe for almost two hours, in the middle of a black-water lagoon near Puerto Nariño, when our guide, Don Ismael, raised his hand. "Listen," he whispered.

At first, I heard nothing but insects. Then came a soft, explosive breath, like a sigh from beneath the water. A few metres away, a pink shape rose to the surface, curved gracefully and disappeared again. Then another. Within minutes, we were surrounded by a family of Amazon river dolphins.

I had seen photographs, of course, but nothing prepared me for the colour — a rosy pink that seemed impossible in nature — or for their curiosity. One young dolphin swam directly under the canoe, turned on its side and appeared to look at us. Whatever it was thinking, I felt, for a moment, that we were the ones being observed.

On the way back, Don Ismael told us that the species is now endangered. Fishermen used to kill them to use as bait, and poaching continues in some areas. Dams and mercury from illegal gold mining are poisoning the rivers. "Wherever there is mining," he said, "the dolphins disappear."

I think about that afternoon whenever I read about the Amazon. Conservation can sound like an abstract word, full of statistics and policies. For me, it now has a face — pink, curious and, for the moment, still breathing.

10.title: Should English be the global language of science?
10.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether it is beneficial or harmful that most scientific research is published in English.
10.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si es positivo o negativo que casi toda la ciencia se publique en inglés.
criteria: A range of passive forms (is published, has been argued, being judged, to be translated).
Correct subject-verb agreement with quantifiers (each of, none of, a number of, the majority of).
Use “mother tongue”, “to get your point across” and “lost in translation”.
10.model:
It has been estimated that more than 90% of articles in the natural sciences are now published in English. For researchers in Colombia, Brazil or China, mastering a foreign language is therefore no longer optional. Is this dominance a benefit or a barrier?

The advantages are clear. A common language allows ideas to be shared across borders instantly. When a vaccine is being developed or a new species is discovered, the findings can be read by scientists everywhere. A number of major breakthroughs have resulted from international collaborations that would have been impossible without a lingua franca.

However, the costs are significant and often overlooked. Researchers whose mother tongue is not English must spend years — and considerable money — learning to write academic prose. Each of these scientists is competing with native speakers who can get their point across with far less effort, and studies show that non-native authors' papers are more likely to be rejected for "language problems". Valuable local knowledge is also being lost: research on Colombian ecosystems or indigenous medicine is sometimes ignored simply because it was published in Spanish. Nuance, too, can be lost in translation.

None of this means that English should be abandoned. The majority of scientists agree that a shared language is indispensable. Yet the system could be made fairer. Journals could accept submissions in several languages and have them translated using AI tools, and editors could be trained to judge papers on their ideas rather than their style. Science, after all, should be measured by what it discovers, not by how fluently it is written.

10.title: Slang, dialects and identity
10.brief: Write an article for a language-learning website about the role of slang and regional dialects in Colombia and what they reveal about identity.
10.briefEs: Escribe un artículo sobre el papel de la jerga y los dialectos regionales en Colombia y lo que revelan sobre la identidad.
criteria: Agreement with quantifiers and collective nouns (everyone, most of the vocabulary, a lot of words).
Three passive constructions.
Use “dialect”, “slang” and “loan word”.
10.model:
Parce, Bacano, Chévere: What Colombian Slang Says About Us

For a country of 52 million people, Colombia has a remarkable variety of ways of speaking. Every region has its own dialect, and almost everyone can identify where a speaker comes from within a few words.

In Medellín, friends are called "parce" — a shortened form of "parcero", which is thought to have come from the word "parcela", or plot of land. In Bogotá, something excellent is "chévere" or "bacano", while on the Caribbean coast, it might be "nítido". People from Cali are known for "ve" and "mirá", which show the influence of the "voseo", a form of address that most of the country abandoned centuries ago.

Much of this vocabulary has been shaped by history. A lot of words in Colombian slang are loan words from English, such as "man" or "parche" (from "patch"), while others come from indigenous languages: "chusco" (attractive) is believed to derive from Quechua. Some expressions were popularised by television series and are now used by speakers who have never been to the regions they come from.

Slang is often dismissed as "bad Spanish", but linguists disagree. Each dialect has its own consistent grammar and sound system. More importantly, the way we speak is a badge of identity. None of the students I teach abroad sounds more "Colombian" than when they slip into regional slang with a friend.

For learners of Spanish, my advice is simple: learn the standard forms, but don't ignore the slang. That is where a language really comes alive.

10.title: How I finally got my tongue around English sounds
10.brief: Write a reflective piece about a specific difficulty you have had with English (pronunciation, phrasal verbs, idioms) and how you have dealt with it.
10.briefEs: Escribe un texto reflexivo sobre una dificultad concreta con el inglés y cómo la has enfrentado.
criteria: Passive forms in at least three different tenses.
Two quantifier subjects with correct agreement (Neither of…, Every one of…).
Use “to get your tongue around”, “to pick up” and “fluent”.
10.model:
For years, there was one sound in English that I simply could not get my tongue around: the "th" in words like "think" and "this". Spanish speakers in Colombia are not used to placing the tongue between the teeth, and every time I tried, I felt ridiculous.

At school, pronunciation was barely taught. We were given lists of vocabulary to memorise and grammar exercises to complete, but none of the lessons was devoted to sounds. As a result, I said "I tink" and "dis" well into my twenties, and I was often misunderstood. Once, at a conference in Toronto, I told a colleague I was "sinking" about his proposal. Neither of us knew where to look.

What changed things was a decision to be recorded. A tutor I found online asked me to read short texts aloud, and every recording was played back with the problem sounds highlighted. Hearing myself was painful, but it worked. I also picked up a trick from a YouTube channel: exaggerating the sound in front of a mirror until it no longer felt strange.

I would not call myself perfectly fluent, and every one of my friends from abroad can still hear my accent. But I no longer feel anxious when I have to say "three thousand". The sound that was once avoided at all costs has been tamed.

The lesson, I think, is that pronunciation is a physical skill, not an intellectual one. It cannot be learned from a book; it has to be practised, repeatedly, out loud.

11.title: Are role models still necessary?
11.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether young people need role models, and whether celebrities and influencers are suitable ones.
11.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si los jóvenes necesitan modelos a seguir y si las celebridades lo son.
criteria: Four compound adjectives (self-taught, world-famous, hard-working, well-known).
One superlative compound adjective (the best-known, the most widely read).
Use “role model”, “to look up to” and “to leave a legacy”.
11.model:
Young people today are surrounded by potential role models. With a few clicks, they can follow world-famous athletes, award-winning scientists and influencers with millions of followers. But do they really need someone to look up to — and, if so, are these the right people?

There is good evidence that role models matter. Children who see someone like them succeed are more likely to believe they can do the same. When Colombian cyclist Egan Bernal won the Tour de France in 2019, cycling clubs across the country reported a surge in young members. Role models can show that success is possible, especially for children from disadvantaged backgrounds, who may have few examples of hard-working professionals around them.

The problem lies in who young people choose. The best-known figures on social media are often famous for their lifestyle rather than their achievements. Their carefully edited, picture-perfect lives can create unrealistic expectations and encourage materialism. Moreover, celebrities are human, and when a well-respected star is involved in a scandal, the disappointment for young fans can be profound.

In my opinion, role models remain valuable, but they need not be famous. Some of the most inspiring examples are found closer to home: a self-taught grandmother who started a business, a teacher who never gave up on difficult students. Such people may not trend on social media, but they leave a legacy that lasts far longer than any viral video. Rather than banning influencers, schools should help young people think critically about the people they choose to admire.

11.title: Nomination for an award
11.brief: Write a letter nominating someone you know for a community award for exceptional people. Describe their achievements and why they deserve recognition.
11.briefEs: Escribe una carta nominando a alguien que conoces a un premio comunitario para personas excepcionales.
criteria: Five compound adjectives, including one superlative compound (the hardest-working, the most far-reaching).
Formal letter structure with a clear recommendation.
Use “against all odds”, “resilient” and “groundbreaking”.
11.model:
Dear Members of the Selection Committee,

I am writing to nominate Doña Rosalba Mosquera for the 2026 Community Hero Award. I have known her for eight years as a neighbour and fellow volunteer, and I can think of no one who deserves this recognition more.

Doña Rosalba, a sixty-two-year-old retired cleaner from Quibdó, arrived in Bogotá in 2001 after being displaced by violence. Against all odds, she rebuilt her life in a city where she knew no one. Ten years ago, she noticed that many children in the neighbourhood were spending their afternoons alone on the streets while their parents worked. With no money and no official support, she opened her own home as an after-school space.

What began as a handful of children doing homework at her kitchen table has grown into a well-organised community centre that serves more than 120 children every week. Her approach was groundbreaking for the area: alongside homework help, she introduced traditional Pacific music and dance classes, which have given many young people a sense of pride in their roots. Several of her former students are now at university.

Doña Rosalba is the hardest-working, most big-hearted person I know. She is resilient but humble, and she always insists that the credit belongs to the volunteers. Her impact on our community has been among the most far-reaching I have witnessed.

I hope you will consider her nomination. I would be happy to provide further information or testimonies from families.

Yours faithfully,
Julián Arango

11.title: Profile: a trailblazer in your field
11.brief: Write a profile of a person who blazed a trail in a field you are interested in (science, sport, art, business), for a website celebrating exceptional people.
11.briefEs: Escribe un perfil de una persona pionera en un campo que te interese para un sitio web sobre personas excepcionales.
criteria: Five compound adjectives, including two before nouns (a record-breaking career).
One superlative compound adjective.
Use “to blaze a trail”, “to overcome” and “determined”.
11.model:
Francisca Ramírez: The Scientist Who Mapped the Invisible

Few people outside the scientific world have heard of Dr. Francisca Ramírez, yet her work has changed the way we understand Colombia's rivers.

Born in a working-class family in Montería, she was the first person in her family to finish secondary school. Determined to study biology, she overcame enormous obstacles: she worked night shifts in a bakery to pay for her studies and taught herself English using second-hand textbooks. "I was largely self-taught," she recalls. "The library was my second home."

In the 1990s, when the study of freshwater microorganisms was considered a niche, low-prestige field, Ramírez blazed a trail. Her ground-breaking research showed that tiny, often invisible organisms could be used to measure the health of entire rivers — a cheap, reliable method that is now used across Latin America. Her long-term study of the Sinú river is one of the most widely cited environmental studies ever produced in the country.

Beyond her research, she has been a tireless, outspoken advocate for women in science. She founded a mentoring network that has supported more than 800 young female researchers from low-income backgrounds.

Now retired, Ramírez remains characteristically modest. When asked about her record-breaking career, she shrugs. "I simply asked questions that nobody else thought were important."

For a generation of Colombian scientists, she is proof that brilliance can come from anywhere — and that the most important discoveries are sometimes the ones nobody else is looking for.

12.title: Is entrepreneurship overrated?
12.brief: Write a discursive essay on whether young people are being encouraged too strongly to start their own businesses instead of seeking stable employment.
12.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo discursivo sobre si se presiona demasiado a los jóvenes para emprender en lugar de buscar empleo estable.
criteria: Two conditionals with inversion (Were…, Had…, Should…).
Three adverb clauses of condition (provided that, unless, as long as, on condition that).
Use “startup”, “to break even” and “to get off the ground”.
12.model:
Social media is full of young founders who claim to have built million-dollar companies from their bedrooms. Universities run entrepreneurship programmes, and governments promote startups as the solution to unemployment. But is this enthusiasm justified?

There are undeniable benefits to entrepreneurship. New businesses create jobs, drive innovation and allow people to pursue their passions. In Colombia, where formal employment is scarce for many graduates, starting a company may be the only way to earn a decent income. Provided that founders have a viable idea and some financial support, the experience of building something can be invaluable, even if the business eventually fails.

However, the risks are rarely discussed honestly. The majority of startups close within five years, and many never break even. Were young people better informed about these statistics, fewer of them would invest their savings — or their parents' — in untested ideas. Getting a business off the ground also requires skills that most graduates have not yet developed: managing cash flow, negotiating with suppliers, hiring staff. Had I started a company at twenty-two, I suspect I would have learned these lessons the hard way.

In my view, entrepreneurship should be presented as one option among many, not as the only path to success. Working for an established organisation first allows people to gain experience and contacts. As long as they keep their ambitions alive, there is nothing to stop them launching their own venture later, with far better chances. Unless we stop glorifying the founder myth, we risk setting a generation up for disappointment.

12.title: Negotiating a better offer
12.brief: You have received a job offer but want to negotiate the conditions (salary, remote work, start date). Write a formal email to the employer.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal negociando las condiciones de una oferta de trabajo (salario, teletrabajo, fecha de inicio).
criteria: One conditional with inversion (Should you need…, Were it possible…).
Two adverb clauses of condition (provided that, on condition that, as long as).
A professional, confident but courteous tone.
12.model:
Dear Ms. Salgado,

Thank you very much for offering me the position of Senior Data Analyst at Andina Logistics. I was delighted to receive your letter, and I remain very enthusiastic about the opportunity to join your team.

Before formally accepting, I would like to discuss two aspects of the offer. Firstly, regarding the salary, I note that the proposed figure is somewhat below the market rate for similar roles in Bogotá, according to recent industry surveys. Given my eight years of experience and my expertise in supply-chain forecasting, I would like to ask whether it would be possible to increase the base salary by 12%. I would be happy to consider a smaller increase provided that it were reviewed after a six-month probation period.

Secondly, I would greatly appreciate the opportunity to work remotely two days a week. In my current role, this arrangement has allowed me to be considerably more productive, and I am confident it would not affect my availability for meetings, as long as these are scheduled in advance.

Were it possible to agree on these points, I would be ready to start on 1 March, as originally planned. Should you need any further information about my previous projects or references, please do not hesitate to contact me.

I look forward to your response and, I hope, to working with you.

Yours sincerely,
Daniel Morales

12.title: The ideal job: a reflective essay
12.brief: Write a personal essay describing your ideal job and the conditions under which you would accept compromises (salary, location, hours).
12.briefEs: Escribe un ensayo personal sobre tu trabajo ideal y bajo qué condiciones aceptarías hacer concesiones.
criteria: Two inverted conditionals and three adverb clauses of condition.
Use “to think outside the box”, “to scale back” and “to be in the black”.
A reflective tone with a thoughtful conclusion.
12.model:
When I was a child, my ideal job changed every week: astronaut, footballer, vet. Today, my answer is less glamorous but considerably more detailed.

My ideal job would allow me to think outside the box. I am happiest when I am solving problems that do not have obvious answers, so I would rather design something new than manage something that already exists. I would also want my work to have a visible impact — ideally in education or public health, where good ideas can change thousands of lives.

The people matter as much as the tasks. I would accept a modest salary on condition that I worked with colleagues who were generous with their knowledge and honest in their criticism. Had I been asked this question five years ago, I would have put money first. Experience has taught me that a toxic team can ruin even the best-paid position.

Of course, ideals have limits. I have to pay rent, and I would like to help my parents in the future. Unless a job paid enough for me to be in the black at the end of each month, I could not take it, however inspiring it was. Should the perfect opportunity appear in another city, I would be willing to move, provided that I could return home regularly.

Perhaps the ideal job is less a fixed destination than a direction. If I ever had to scale back my ambitions, I would hope to do so without losing sight of why I started: to do work that matters, with people I respect.
